The user wants to list every cohort with its owner and how many subjects it holds, as a table.

Looking at the catalog, cohorts have these fields:
- id: integer
- name: text
- owner: text
- members: integer (this represents the number of subjects)

So I need to:
1. Create a cohort set at grain: cohort
2. Get the subject count - but wait, members is already in the cohort data

Actually, looking at the catalog more carefully:
```json
{"cohorts":[{"id":1,"name":"ms-cohort-a","owner":"nils-synth","members":38},{"id":2,"name":"ms-cohort-b","owner":"nils-synth","members":12}]}
```

The "members" field directly gives the count of subjects in each cohort. So I can use that field directly.

Let me construct the document:
- sets:
  - cohorts: grain: cohort (with all fields we need)
- out:
  - set: cohorts
  - level: record
  - columns: [[field, name], [field, owner], [field, members]]
  - order: [[[field, name], asc]]

This is straightforward - no need to create a separate subject set since members is already tracked in the cohort.
